sources.product: Automatically extracted rock outcrop dataset for Antarctica, version 7.3 (SCAR Antarctic Digital Database)
sources.producer: L. Gerrish, UK Polar Data Centre (British Antarctic Survey); method by Burton-Johnson et al. 2016
sources.coverage: Antarctica, 60°S to 90°S; Landsat 8 method north of 82°40'S, older ADD outcrops south of it (paper)
sources.resolution_spatial: vector polygons; Landsat pixel size not stated on page
sources.uncertainty: no figure on the pages read; the paper finds exposed rock is 0.18% of Antarctica (21,745 km2), half of previous estimates
sources.limitations: Two DOIs on the record (178ec50d... and 9DF510E3...); shaded snow is the known confusion of simpler indices. Fills the gap south of 60°S, where WorldCover has no tile (T40): everything outside the polygons is ice or snow
sources.attribution: Gerrish, L. (2020). Automatically extracted rock outcrop dataset for Antarctica (7.3). UK Polar Data Centre, NERC, UKRI. doi:10.5285/9DF510E3-EA1C-450B-9950-D742DB1EFD96; method: Burton-Johnson et al. (2016), The Cryosphere 10, 1665-1677

sources.product: Natural Earth Admin 0 - Countries, 1:110m (GeoJSON, nvkelso/natural-earth-vector, master branch on 18/11/2026)
sources.coverage: global, 177 countries with a CONTINENT field (7 continents plus open ocean)
sources.uncertainty: not stated on page; coasts generalised at 1:110m
sources.limitations: Used only to count results by continent (bias check of the validation protocol); cells on generalised coasts stay unassigned
sources.attribution: Made with Natural Earth. Free vector and raster map data @ naturalearthdata.com

sources.product: SLDEM2015 merged elevation model (Barker et al. 2016)
sources.resolution_spatial: 512 pixels per degree (about 60 m at the equator)
sources.limitations: No polar coverage; read the README for accuracy

sources.product: Reduced spectrometer data, special products (Fe, Ti, Th, K, H, O, Si, Al, Mg, Ca, U, Sm, neutron rates)
sources.producer: LP Spectrometer Team (LANL and partners); not a peer-reviewed PDS archive
sources.resolution_spatial: bins of 0.5°, 2° (60 km) and 5° (150 km), depending on the element
sources.resolution_effective: not stated on page; at least the bin size
sources.uncertainty: standard deviation provided only for neutron rates and some Th products
sources.limitations: Hydrogen derived from epithermal neutrons, 'not necessarily reliable' where Th and rare earths are high

sources.product: Unified Geologic Map of the Moon, 1:5M, 2020 (edition 2.0, 3 March 2020)
sources.producer: C. M. Fortezzo (USGS), P. D. Spudis (LPI), S. L. Harrel (SD Mines); USGS Astrogeology Science Center
sources.resolution_spatial: 1:5,000,000; vertices about 3 km apart, smoothed with a tolerance of about 16 km
sources.uncertainty: attribute accuracy: best effort; horizontal position: accurate to the LOLA control net
sources.limitations: Photogeologic units, not measured composition; subject to update after community review. Cite Fortezzo, Spudis and Harrel (2020), LPSC 51, abstract 2760. page read in a browser by David on 18/11/2026 (host refuses automated reading)

sources.coverage: 278 pits listed on the list page (read 18/11/2026, T41), 72°N to 78°S
sources.limitations: List page read (278 pits: host feature, position, diameters, depth with lower bounds); the PDF (over 10 MB) and the terms of use not read. Hosts are named features, not settings: 229 pits lie in Copernican crater units of the geologic map (T41)

sources.resolution_effective: coarser than 40 m away from the pole: grid interpolated between laser tracks (finding L3, not quantified)
sources.limitations: Interpolation between tracks; includes shadowed crater walls and floors

sources.product: Polar average solar illumination, permanent shadow, Earth and sky visibility (Mazarico et al. 2011, R6)
sources.coverage: 65°S to 90°S at 240 m, 75°S to 90°S at 120 m, 85°S to 90°S at 60 m; north equivalents
sources.limitations: Computed from topography, not observed; some download links point to the wrong file type

sources.product: Macrostrat API v2 and map tiles
sources.coverage: multi-scale compilation; global coverage varies by region
sources.limitations: Live API: results must be frozen in a snapshot to stay reproducible; API v3 not for published work
sources.attribution: Macrostrat, CC-BY 4.0; cite the original map sources returned with each record

sources.product: Ground Temperature Map 2000-2016, Northern Hemisphere Permafrost (Obu et al. 2018 data; paper R32)
sources.limitations: Model; replaces the air-temperature proxy for frozen ground (v2 decision E4)

sources.product: Global Aridity Index and Potential Evapotranspiration Database, version 3.1 (Global-AI_PET_v3); v3.0 is deprecated
sources.uncertainty: not stated on page; v3.0 had a dry bias from a net longwave error, corrected in v3.1
sources.limitations: Use v3.1 only. Climatology of 1970 to 2000, not current conditions; no interannual sigma. Page read in a browser by David on 18/11/2026 (host refuses automated reading); file list, licence and MD5 from the figshare API (api.figshare.com/v2/articles/7504448) on 20/11/2026
sources.attribution: Zomer, R.J.; Xu, J.; Trabucco, A. 2022. Version 3 of the Global Aridity Index and Potential Evapotranspiration Database. Scientific Data 9, 409
sources.licence: CC BY 4.0 (figshare API, 20/11/2026; the page read on 18/11 was noted as non-commercial)

processing.what: 90 m windows (Copernicus GLO-90) select the 1° tiles refined per target
1 km windows at the lunar pixel of each target (Copernicus GLO-30)
windows whose ground is hidden are excluded (WorldCover 2021; rock outcrops south of 60°S)
two-sided percentile of each window's mean slope among the lunar windows
HEALPix cells (NSIDE 1303, 25.04 km²), one global equal-area grid

rules.climbing_limit_lrv: LRV 20 to 23°, max 25° (NTRS 20250011301); 20° used, the stored lower bound; half of the window (E1)
rules.climbing_limit_viper: VIPER 15° not verified (E1); reported, never eliminating
